rationale: Evaluating omission of required braking requires characterising both the need to brake and whether the required braking response occurs. H-1, SG-1 and FR-7 establish that response itself as part of the evaluation, not merely as a mechanism affecting it. H-1’s failure to stop in time and FR-7.1’s braking-initiation requirement also support considering when braking begins. The scope includes detected-obstacle response conditions without incorporating sensing algorithms, internal decision computations or communication mechanisms.
determining_elements: “The vehicle’s need to brake” identifies the condition against which omission of a required maneuver must be evaluated.
“The braking response relevant to avoiding collision” is directly supported by SG-1 and FR-7.

“Whether and when to initiate braking” concerns the required response and its timing, supported by H-1 and FR-7.1; obstacle detection supplies a response-triggering event rather than expanding P to detection mechanisms.
The declared road, speed, weather and pedestrian-crossing conditions match H-1’s operational situation.
